entries.title: Leviticus 20:2
segments:
Molech; an idol of the Ammonites to whom children were sacrificed. According to the Rabbins his statue was of brass and hollow; and this being heated from below, the children to be sacrificed were put into its arms. 
 
Capital punishment by the hand of magistrates is sometimes not only right, but a duty which they owe to God and their fellow-men.  It is a needful means of restraining iniquity; and the people, when God commands it, are bound to see that it is executed.

entries.title: Leviticus 20:5
segments: If the magistrates and people neglect to prosecute criminals, and to punish the guilty, they encourage crime, incur guilt, and expose themselves to divine judgments.

entries.title: Leviticus 20:8
segments: Sanctify you; separate them from other nations, and set them apart for himself.

entries.title: Leviticus 20:9
segments: That laws should be needful to keep parents from destroying children, and children from cursing parents; and people to whom Jehovah is known from forsaking him for idols, and committing the most polluting and degrading abominations, shows the strength and malignancy of sin, and the necessity, in order to salvation,of being delivered from it by the mighty power of God.
